newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bulls set to yield to bears on German share market.
newsitem.headline: Bulls set to yield to bears on German share market.

text.p: The bull-run seen on German share markets in the fourth quarter of 1996 is tailing off, the bears are in the ascendant and, in the long term, Germany's DAX-30 index will sink, chartists predict.

These technicial analysts say however that the bulls have not quite finished their run and the short-term could still see the psychologically-important 2,900 point threshold on the DAX convincingly penetrated before any consolidation.
The DAX index ended bourse trade on Monday at 2,881.32 points, up 22.04 or 0.77 percent, not too far off 2,900-points.
"Short-term I think the market will break the psychologically-important 2,900-point level -- the upward trend is still intact," said Giro Olbertz, chartist at Vereins- und Westbank.
Marcel Muessler, chartist at DG Bank in Frankfurt, agrees that there is room for the DAX to go above 2,900 points.
"In the short-term there is still breathing space in the market, but once the DAX goes above 2,916 points, the air starts to get thinner," said Muessler.
Not all chartists are agreed on how long the bulls can run for. Ingo Mainert, Commerzbank chartist, says the end is nigh.
"In the short-term I see a downward trend, with 2,900 points as the psychological resistance point. This downward trend could kick in over the next week or two," said Mainert.
Mainert's forecasts are based on momentum indicators, and the current difficulty in assessing market sentiment.

"DAX options on the DTB (German futures and options exchange) are pessimistic, while options on DAX shares are showing signs of optimism. Overall, this divergence shows there is not a great deal of pessimism around," said Mainert.
This means that there is no apparent danger of a serious correction on a technical basis until the index moved below the 2,800-point level, he said.
However, there were technical danger signals coming from the financial markets and as such, Mainert said he does not foresee a move above the magic 3,000-point mark.
According to Marcel Muessler, the main technical signs of an imminent correction are coming from the debt market, although he believes the correction will not come today or tomorrow.
"The debt market is a bad influence, and we could see some kind of overnight surprise. Any kind of correction we see will not be of the order of 10 percent though," said Muessler.
By the end of the first quarter of this year, Muessler expects the DAX to have consolidated to around 2,600/2,650 points.

"The clearest evidence for a correction comes from the debt market, based on weekly Relative Strength Indicators, momentum indicators and Moving Average Convergence-Divergence (MACD) indicators," said Muessler, referring to three of the main indicators used by technical chartists.
Meanwhile, Giro Olbertz expects the correction to take place in the second half of the year.

"The market could rise to around 3,200 points or 3,400 points during the first six months of the year. We could see a correction in the second-half of the year which could see the DAX closing at a lower level than it finished at in 1996 -- around 2,600/2,700 points," said Olbertz.

"I think we are heading for a consolidation period for the year as a whole. Towards the end of the year we see support at 2,850 and resistance at 2,850 points, with the market ending the year at 2,750 points," said Mainert.
